the_bottleneck: The Tennessee OSM index build: about 70 minutes of wall clock for a 189 MB extract, run while another market's full broad regression held the CPU. It is a one-time cost per region and it overlapped the free lead lanes, so it did not gate the market; the second longest single wait was the destination bureau's own Crawl-delay of 2 seconds over about 190 pages, roughly 7 minutes, and that is politeness rather than inefficiency.
what_made_this_fast: the Tennessee extract was already on disk in the Nashville worktree; no download
the committed Dayton brand harvest gave 19 Marriott Chattanooga-area routes at ZERO requests
Hilton's own city page gave 20 CTYHOCN codes, addresses and slugs in ONE request
the attended lane read 48 walled property pages in TWO same-origin navigations
dumping the attended results into the page's own DOM and reading them with get_page_text beat chunked JavaScript returns, which truncate at about 1 KB
